solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: We raise rule for ordering casual clothing

indicators.note: ordering means putting these clue letters into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Someone lifting a dress-code rule so people can turn up in relaxed clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordering' tells you to rearrange WE RAISE RULE; 'for' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisurewear is relaxed, informal attire worn when not working, so casual clothing describes it directly.

clue.text: Friend supporting English queen on a fair basis

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece supporting another sits beneath it, so it comes after

parts.note: an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A loyal companion backing an English monarch fairly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts ALLY under E QU in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on a fair basis means everyone gets the same share, which is acting evenly.

clue.text: Depot and base renovated marine vehicle

indicators.note: renovated means done up and remade, so the letters of these two words are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A depot and a naval base have been refurbished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renovated' rearranges DEPOT and BASE together; 'and' joins the fodder words but adds no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A speedboat is a fast motor boat, a vehicle that travels on the sea.

clue.text: Summarise return of fast athlete?

indicators.note: return of means the word for the athlete is read backwards

parts.note: a pacer is a runner who sets a fast pace; the question mark flags the loose definition

explanation.surface: A sprinter coming back to give a quick summary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' turns PACER round.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to go over the main points again briefly, which is to summarise.

clue.text: Financial support providing mostly satisfactory food

indicators.note: mostly means the word for satisfactory loses its final letter

parts.note: well can mean satisfactory, as in 'all is well'
fare means food, as in 'simple fare'

explanation.surface: Benefits that provide meals that are fairly decent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts WELL to WEL; 'providing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Welfare is state money paid to those in need, a form of financial support.

clue.text: Johnson, say, a winner, one having replaced leader of charisma

indicators.note: having replaced means one letter is swapped in for another in the word for winner

parts.note: a victor is a winner

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter of charisma

parts.note: one can be the indefinite article a

explanation.surface: A tribute to a champion called Johnson who somehow lost her charisma.
explanation.walkthrough: Amy Johnson was a pioneering English pilot of the 1930s; 'Johnson, say' looks like a name to place, but it is an example. 'having replaced' swaps the C (leader of charisma) for the A meaning 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Amy Johnson was a famous pilot, so she is an example of a flyer of aircraft.

clue.text: Manufacture of a prime cheap material

indicators.note: manufacture of means the following letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: Producing a top-quality but inexpensive fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manufacture of' rearranges A PRIME CHEAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Papier-mache is a modelling substance of pulped paper and paste, a craft material.

clue.text: Wonder created by English poet in audience

indicators.note: in audience means as heard by listeners, so the poet's name is said aloud

parts.note: Andrew Marvell was a seventeenth-century English poet

explanation.surface: A marvel produced by a poet when he reads to listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in audience' signals a homophone: MARVELL, the poet, sounds like the answer, which drops one L.
explanation.definitionFit: A marvel is something amazing, and as a verb to marvel is to wonder at it.

clue.text: Usually characteristic of a period in office?

definitions.meaning: generally, in the normal course of things

definitions.text: characteristic of a period in office?
definitions.meaning: whimsically, like a reign or spell of ruling

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means normally or generally, and read literally it describes a time spent ruling.

clue.text: French place in island beset by cold sadly

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the island letter sits inside the word for sadly

parts.note: alas expresses sorrow, used for sadly

explanation.surface: A French town, on an island hemmed in by sad cold weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beset by' puts I inside ALAS after C; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Calais is a port town in northern France facing Dover across the Channel.

clue.text: Versatile sportsman leapt the net fantastically

indicators.note: fantastically suggests wild transformation, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An athlete jumped over the tennis net in astonishing style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastically' rearranges LEAPT THE NET.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentathlete competes in five different events, so must be an all-round athlete.

clue.text: Popular boxer in very short end to round lacking force?

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: in places the boxer within the letters around him

parts.note: very short means very abbreviated, so V

indicators.note: end to means the last letter of round

parts.note: Muhammad Ali, the famous boxer

explanation.surface: A well-loved fighter, at the very end of a round, has no strength left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the boxer between V and D (end to round). The question mark is because the legal sense, not valid, means without force.
explanation.definitionFit: Something invalid has no legal force or weight, as a void contract does.

clue.text: Piano used by conductor giving empty talk

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
Sir Simon Rattle is a famous British conductor

explanation.surface: A conductor using a piano and talking pointlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used by' is a link here, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Prattle is foolish, childish chatter, talk with nothing behind it.

clue.text: Athletics event is broadcast

definitions.meaning: a team race where runners pass a baton
to transmit a signal or programme onwards

explanation.definitionFit: A team race passing a baton has this name, and it also means to pass on a transmission.

clue.text: Like a horse ride without a break?

definitions.meaning: a horse moving at a trot, faster than a walk

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in succession, and literally describes a horse going at a trot.

clue.text: Strategic expert showing diplomacy in charge with Scotsman

parts.note: tact is diplomacy in handling people
Ian is a typical Scottish first name

explanation.surface: A Scot in command who is very diplomatic and good at planning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactician is skilled at planning moves to gain advantage, a strategy expert.

clue.text: Genuine source of arbitration disputed in the TUC

indicators.note: source of means the first letter of arbitration
disputed suggests something argued over and unsettled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Real arbitration being challenged inside the Trades Union Congress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of' gives A; 'disputed' rearranges IN THE TUC. The TUC is Britain's Trades Union Congress. 'in' looks like a link but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something authentic is real and not a copy, which is what genuine means.

clue.text: Plant obtained by company following revolutionary explorer

indicators.note: following means the company comes after the explorer
revolutionary means turned round, so the explorer's name is read backwards

parts.note: John Cabot was a Venetian explorer who sailed for England

explanation.surface: A plant obtained by a firm after a radical explorer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns CABOT to TOBAC; 'obtained by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobacco is a leafy plant grown for smoking, so it is a plant.

clue.text: Further tips for contentment in part of work?

parts.note: extra means further or additional

indicators.note: tips for means the first and last letters of contentment

explanation.surface: More advice on being content in some section of one's job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tips for' gives C and T. The question mark is because work here means a book or composition.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract is a passage taken from a longer piece of writing, a portion of a work.

clue.text: Musical composition captured in session one time

indicators.note: captured in means the answer is held within these words

explanation.surface: A piece of music recorded in one session at one time.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a piece written for nine instruments or voices.

clue.text: Source of retribution is occupying Kent chaps on reflection

indicators.note: on reflection means the whole assembly is seen as in a mirror, read backwards
occupying means the word is sits inside the region abbreviation

parts.note: Kent is in the South East of England, abbreviated SE
taken as written
men are chaps

explanation.surface: Kent men looking back on a figure of vengeance moving in among them.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in South East England, hence SE. 'occupying' puts IS inside SE, and 'on reflection' reverses the whole SISEMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis was the Greek goddess of retribution, so the word means an agent of downfall.

clue.text: Bite to consider reportedly in country

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the words are spoken aloud

parts.note: gnaw means bite and weigh means consider; said together they make the answer's sound

explanation.surface: A nibble to ponder, as said, in some nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' signals a homophone: GNAW WEIGH, said aloud. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Norway is a Scandinavian nation on the west of the peninsula, a country.

clue.text: A short time in Panama, say, for the environment

indicators.note: in means the short time goes inside the headgear

parts.note: a Panama is a type of straw hat
a bit is a short time, as in 'wait a bit'

explanation.surface: A short time spent in Panama, enjoying the surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panama' is capitalised to suggest the country, but it is the straw hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural home of an animal or plant, its surroundings.

clue.text: Journeys made by king entering very French surroundings

indicators.note: entering means the king goes inside the French word; 'surroundings' backs this up

parts.note: tres is French for very
K is the chess notation for king

explanation.surface: Travels undertaken by a monarch arriving in very French settings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' puts K inside TRES; 'surroundings' only reinforces that the French word encloses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Treks are long, arduous journeys, often on foot.

clue.text: Small measure taken before exam? That's wrong

parts.note: 1 MM, one millimetre, is a small measure of length
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: Measuring something tiny before a test is unethical.
explanation.walkthrough: The small measure is read as 1 MM, the digit 1 standing for I. 'taken before' just orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Immoral means not conforming to accepted ethics, so morally wrong.

clue.text: What fiddler does in predicament

definitions.meaning: a violinist draws the bow across the strings
a tight spot or awkward situation

explanation.definitionFit: A violinist draws a bow harshly across strings, and a tight spot is also a mess one gets into.

clue.text: Second type of coffee?

definitions.meaning: a moment, a very short time

explanation.definitionFit: A moment is an extremely brief time, and quick soluble coffee made by adding water shares the name.

clue.text: Sushi stolen in buffet? It's ill-bred behaviour

indicators.note: buffet as a verb means knock about, so these letters are battered into a new order

explanation.surface: Stealing raw fish from a self-service spread is rude conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buffet' looks like the food table, but it is the verb meaning batter, rearranging SUSHI STOLEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Loutishness is the rough, rude conduct of a lout, so it means boorish behaviour.
